paragraphs: The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is the first with a Dynamic Island. The interactive, pill-shaped module is borrowed from the iPhone, but where’s the iPhone’s Face ID? Apple left it out — and some Mac fans are mad.

On the iPhone, the Dynamic Island wraps around the TrueDepth camera that powers Face ID. But not on this pricey MacBook Pro — Touch ID still handles login authentication. Instead of the laptop unlocking magically when users look at it, they will need to give it the finger instead.

On the new MacBook Pro, which Apple unveiled Wednesday, the Dynamic Island replaces the familiar screen notch with an interactive hub for notifications, music and Siri. And the laptop’s touchscreen — the first ever on a Mac — makes tapping those controls feel more natural than ever.

Yet even on a laptop costing thousands of dollars, unlocking the machine still requires Touch ID rather than the effortless glance that Face ID offers on the iPhone. The curious omission exposes a weird gap in Apple’s ecosystem: While the company spent years making its devices feel more seamlessly connected, some of its best everyday conveniences remain stubbornly confined to individual products.

At MacBook Pro prices, fans aren’t just asking for a flashy new display. They want the whole experience to feel top of the line. Face ID would offer a more seamless way to unlock a Mac than Touch ID because it authenticates you with a simple glance, without requiring you to touch a button or position a finger correctly.
The redesigned MacBook Pro comes in 14-inch and 16-inch models. On both models, the Dynamic Island replaces the notch from previous MBP models.

Apple says the Dynamic Island is the new home for Spotlight, Live Activities and Siri AI. You can also answer a call or control music. And thanks to the touchscreen, a single tap can accept an AirDrop request or pause a song. (According to Apple’s fine print, Spotlight only works in the Dynamic Island if Siri AI is available and enabled.)
The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display isn’t a cheap laptop. The 14-inch model with an M5 Pro processor starts at $2,899. The 16-inch version starts at $3,399.
